sections.title: Objects and components
sections.text:
# Objects and components

UnityEngine.Object, GameObject, Component and Transform expose the M20 source surface over the same native identities, lifecycle and scene as the retained Axiom.Gameplay API. Their public vectors and rotations use floats. Other API areas continue to use their documented namespaces until their milestones are accepted. A declaration match is separate from per-overload behavior certification.

Runtime transforms retain full affine matrices, including shear and zero-scale local coordinates. Authored reparenting still rejects shear that cannot be saved as plain TRS. Runtime changes are discarded on Stop. Runtime cloning snapshots serialized fields and references; asynchronous clones defer scene activation, support cancellation and use the owned integration queue. Explicit limits remain 65,536 entities, 32 attached physical scripts and 128 wire operations per phase.

CreatePrimitive creates owned Sphere, Capsule, Cylinder, Cube, Plane and Quad mesh assets and the corresponding MeshFilter, MeshRenderer and collider. Capsule and Cylinder use a capsule collider; Plane and Quad use finite one-sided mesh surfaces in the Rust CPU solver. Normal runtime scenes expose Unity 6.3’s documented default scene culling mask; editor preview-scene mask controls belong to the later editor milestone.

Mesh, render and collider facades supplied as M20 dependencies expose their implemented members only; their full API areas remain separate milestones. Unsupported asset cloning or component construction fails explicitly. See the generated namespace comments and the exact source before using an API.

Execution and time
sections.text:
# Execution and time

At Play start all initially active scripts receive Awake, then OnEnable, then Start. Scripts added/cloned at runtime receive Awake and OnEnable immediately, and Start before their first update. Disabled behaviours skip Update/FixedUpdate/LateUpdate; deactivating their GameObject also stops coroutines. OnDisable precedes OnDestroy. All Update callbacks finish before LateUpdate begins.

Each real fixed step invokes FixedUpdate, advances the native solver once at 1/60 second, dispatches contacts and resumes WaitForFixedUpdate. Variable Update and coroutines then run, followed by global LateUpdate/end-of-frame waits. Physics has an eight-step catch-up cap. Axiom callbacks are explicit public virtual overrides; Unity private message dispatch is not implemented.

Time supports scaled and unscaled frame time and timeScale in [0,8]. At zero scale Update and unscaled waits continue; physics, scaled waits and Invoke pause. Coroutines support nested IEnumerator, yield null, WaitForSeconds, WaitForSecondsRealtime, WaitUntil, WaitWhile, WaitForFixedUpdate, WaitForEndOfFrame and waiting on Coroutine handles. Invoke/InvokeRepeating accept compiled parameterless void methods; cancellation and query are available. There is no string-based StartCoroutine or arbitrary async Unity resource yield instruction.

sections.text:
# Mathematics

Axiom.Gameplay API reference. Unity naming baseline: Unity 6.3 LTS.

Existing PascalCase names remain supported. Lowercase vector fields and constants are available. Vector numbers use double rather than Unity float. Vector4Int is an Axiom extension. Legacy Vector3.Forward points toward -Z; the Unity-compatible lowercase Vector3.forward points +Z. Axiom cameras look along local -Z. Random wraps the deterministic replay generator; qualify Axiom.Gameplay.Random when System.Random is also in scope. Not every Unity math member is implemented.

# Color

Namespace: `Axiom.Gameplay`

## Description

## Use cases

Store a tint in an exposed script field.

## Example

The statements below belong inside a `MonoBehaviour` callback. Add the components/resources mentioned in the use case first.

```csharp
var tint = new Color(0.2, 0.5, 1, 1);
Debug.Log(tint.B);
```

Existing PascalCase names remain supported. Lowercase vector fields and constants are available. Vector numbers use double rather than Unity float. Vector4Int is an Axiom extension. sections.title: Rigidbody
RigidBody
sections.text:
# RigidBody

Namespace: `Axiom.Gameplay`

## Description

Legacy immutable velocity snapshot. Reading it does not provide a writable component; use Entity.SetVelocity or the live Rigidbody/Rigidbody2D facade to mutate the body.

## Use cases

Preserve vertical speed in existing Axiom controllers.

## Example

The statements below belong inside a `MonoBehaviour` callback. Add the components/resources mentioned in the use case first.

```csharp
var velocity = Entity.RigidBody.Velocity;
Entity.SetVelocity(new Vector3(2, velocity.Y, velocity.Z));
```

## Compatibility and limitations

RigidBody is the legacy velocity snapshot; Rigidbody is the live wrapper. AddForce uses the current frame delta for force/acceleration and directly applies impulse/velocity change; mass comes from the runtime body. Collider bounds return the solver-aligned world AABB of configured spheres/boxes, including orientation. Collider half-extents are already world units and are not multiplied by visual Transform scale. Raycasts use the current sphere/oriented-box solver baseline, layer filtering and a finite default 1000-unit distance; triggers are included. Capsules/meshes currently use their configured box collider. Contact callbacks consume the preceding completed physics snapshot (up to 128 contacts), so delivery is one render frame later and omitted contacts cannot emit callbacks. Full Unity Collision.contacts, joints and arbitrary shape casts remain pending.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
// Namespace: Axiom.Gameplay
public readonly record struct RigidBody(Vector3 Velocity) {
 internal static RigidBody Read(JsonElement value) => new(Vector3.Read(value.GetProperty("velocity")));
}
```

sections.text:
# ForceMode

Namespace: `Axiom.Gameplay`

## Description

Selects how Rigidbody.AddForce changes velocity: Force divides by mass and integrates over deltaTime; Acceleration omits mass; Impulse divides by mass without a time factor; VelocityChange omits both.

## Use cases

Apply an instantaneous jump or a sustained acceleration.

## Example

The statements below belong inside a `MonoBehaviour` callback. Add the components/resources mentioned in the use case first.

```csharp
var body = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
if (body != null) body.AddForce(Vector3.up * 5, ForceMode.VelocityChange);
```

## Compatibility and limitations

RigidBody is the legacy velocity snapshot; Rigidbody is the live wrapper. AddForce uses the current frame delta for force/acceleration and directly applies impulse/velocity change; mass comes from the runtime body. Collider bounds return the solver-aligned world AABB of configured spheres/boxes, including orientation. Collider half-extents are already world units and are not multiplied by visual Transform scale. Raycasts use the current sphere/oriented-box solver baseline, layer filtering and a finite default 1000-unit distance; triggers are included. Capsules/meshes currently use their configured box collider. Contact callbacks consume the preceding completed physics snapshot (up to 128 contacts), so delivery is one render frame later and omitted contacts cannot emit callbacks. Full Unity Collision.contacts, joints and arbitrary shape casts remain pending.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
// Namespace: Axiom.Gameplay
public enum ForceMode {Force,Acceleration,Impulse,VelocityChange}
```

Derive a custom wait with public override bool keepWaiting. The scheduler checks it once per Update after at least one frame.
